title: Inconsistent Reads (Read Skew)
pattern: Reading different elements of a shared state structure sequentially without holding a common lock or using a single atomic transaction.
why_bad: The state reads are temporally uncoordinated, resulting in a read skew where the individual read values represent inconsistent snapshots of the system.
detection: Sequential non-synchronized reads on dependent data members where writes to those members are synchronized.
counterexample: `Context-dependent`: If the system does not require strict transactional consistency, skew may be acceptable.
source: Martin Fowler (PEEAA) Ch 15, Alex Petrov Ch 5
